title.en: Volume 91: Rhythm and the Calendar Part Two
title.raw: 第二 律曆中 賈逵論曆 永元論曆 延光論曆 漢安論曆 熹平論曆 論月食 Volume 91: Rhythm and the Calendar Part Two

sentences.zh: 後漢書志第二 律歷中 賈逵論歷永元論歷延光論歷漢安論歷熹平論歷論月食

translations.literal: Book of Later Han, Treatise Two: Pitch-Pipes and Calendar, Part Two — On Jia Kui Discussing the Calendar, On the Yongyuan Discussion of the Calendar, On the Yanguang Discussion of the Calendar, On the Han'an Discussion of the Calendar, On the Xiping Discussion of the Calendar, On Lunar Eclipses
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Two of the Book of Later Han: Music and Calendars, Part Two — Treatises on Jia Kui's calendar memorials and the debates under Yongyuan, Yanguang, Han'an, and Xiping, together with the discussion of lunar eclipses

sentences.zh: 自太初元年始用三統曆，施行百有餘年，歷稍後天，朔先*[於]*歷，朔或在晦，月*[或朔]*見。

translations.literal: From the first year of the Taichu reign they began to use the Triple Concordance calendar; it had been in use for more than a hundred years when the calendar gradually lagged behind heaven, the new moons came earlier than the calendar, new moons sometimes fell on the last day of the month, and the moon was sometimes visible at the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Triple Concordance calendar had been in force since Taichu year 1, but after more than a century it no longer kept pace with the sky: conjunctions came ahead of the official reckoning, sometimes landing on the final day of the month, and the thin crescent could appear when the calendar still called it new moon.

sentences.zh: 考其行，日有退無進，月有進無退。

translations.literal: Examining their motions, the sun had retreat but no advance, and the moon had advance but no retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When one traced their apparent motions, the sun seemed only to fall behind the tabulated motion, never to gain on it, while the moon always ran ahead and never fell short.

sentences.zh: 建武八年中，太僕朱浮﹑太中大夫許淑等數上書，言歷*[朔]*不正，宜當改更。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Jianwu era, the Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia Zhu Fu, the Grand Counselor of the Palace Xu Shu, and others repeatedly submitted memorials saying that the calendar and new-moon predictions were incorrect and ought to be revised.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 8, Chamberlain Zhu Fu and Palace Counselor Xu Shu kept petitioning the throne: the official calendar’s lunations were wrong and needed reform.

sentences.zh: 時分度覺差尚微，上以天下初定，未遑考正。

translations.literal: At that time the discrepancies in divisions and degrees were still slight, and because the realm had only just been pacified, the emperor had no leisure to examine and correct them.
translations.idiomatic: The errors were still small on the scale of fractional degrees, and with the empire only newly settled the emperor set calendar revision aside for the moment.

sentences.zh: 至永平五年，官歷署七月十六日*[月]*食。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of the Yongping era, the official calendar placed a lunar eclipse on the sixteenth day of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping 5 the state calendar predicted a lunar eclipse on the sixteenth of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 待詔楊岑見時月食多先歷，即縮用筭上為日，*[因]*上言「月當十五日食，官歷不中」。

translations.literal: The expectancy-holder Yang Cen observed that lunar eclipses of the time mostly occurred earlier than the calendar said; he therefore shortened the reckoning on the counting-rods by one day for the sun and accordingly memorialized, saying, "The moon ought to be eclipsed on the fifteenth; the official calendar misses it."
translations.idiomatic: Expectancy-holder Yang Cen noticed eclipses were consistently early relative to the official tables; he adjusted the solar count by one day on his rods and reported that the eclipse should fall on the fifteenth while the government calendar was wrong.

sentences.zh: 詔書令岑普*[候]*，與官*[歷]*課。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Cen and Pu to observe and to compete against the official calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yang Cen and Pu to make observations and pit their results against the bureau’s calendar.

sentences.zh: 起七月，盡十一月，弦望凡五，官歷皆失，岑皆中。

translations.literal: From the seventh month through the eleventh month there were in all five quarter- and full-moon junctures; on every one the official calendar failed and Cen hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh month to the eleventh there were five key lunations; the official calendar missed every prediction while Cen’s matched observation each time.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔*[書]*令岑署弦望月食官，復令待詔張盛﹑景防﹑鮑鄴等以四分法與岑課。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day an edict ordered Cen to take charge of quarter-moons, full moons, and lunar eclipses in the office, and further ordered the expectancy-holders Zhang Sheng, Jing Fang, Bao Ye, and others to compete against Cen using the quarter-day method.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Cen was put in charge of predicting quarters, full moons, and eclipses, while Zhang Sheng, Jing Fang, Bao Ye, and fellow expectancy-holders were told to test their quarter-remainder system against him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，盛等所中多岑六事。

translations.literal: After more than a year, among hits Zhang Sheng’s party exceeded Cen by six instances.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year, Zhang Sheng’s group had six more successful predictions than Cen.

sentences.zh: 十二年十一月丙子，詔書令盛﹑防代岑署弦望月食加時。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day of the eleventh month of the twelfth year, an edict ordered Sheng and Fang to replace Cen in determining the times of quarter-moons, full moons, and lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Jianwu 12, on bingzi day, Zhang Sheng and Jing Fang were appointed to succeed Cen in timing quarters, full moons, and eclipses.

sentences.zh: 四分之術，始頗施行。

translations.literal: The quarter-day technique began to be applied on a considerable scale.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time the quarter-remainder system saw substantial official use.

sentences.zh: 是時盛﹑防等未能分明歷元，綜校分度，故但用其弦望而已。

translations.literal: At this time Sheng, Fang, and the others had not yet been able to clarify the calendar epoch or systematically collate the fractional degrees, so they used only its quarter- and full-moon positions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng and Jing Fang had not yet fixed the epoch or reconciled the degree scale, so in practice they relied on the quarter-remainder method only for first and last quarters and full moons.

sentences.zh: 先是，九年，太史待詔董萌上言歷不正，事下三公﹑太常知歷者雜議，訖十年四月，無能分明據者。

translations.literal: Before this, in the ninth year, the Grand Astrologer’s expectancy-holder Dong Meng submitted a memorial saying the calendar was not correct; the matter was sent down to the Three Dukes and the Grand Master of Ceremonies for a mixed discussion among those who knew the calendar, and down to the fourth month of the tenth year there was no one who could provide a clear basis.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in year 9, expectancy-holder Dong Meng of the Grand Astrologer’s office had argued the calendar was faulty; the case went to the Three Dukes and the court experts, but by the fourth month of year 10 no one had produced a conclusive argument.

sentences.zh: 至元和二年，太初失天益遠，日﹑月宿度相覺浸多，而候者皆知冬至之日日在斗二十一度，未至牽牛五度，而以為牽牛中星，*

translations.literal: By the second year of the Yuanhe era, the Taichu system’s deviation from the sky had grown still greater, and the sun’s and moon’s lodge-degrees were felt to diverge more and more; those who observed all knew that on the day of the winter solstice the sun was at 21° in the Dipper, not yet 5° into the Ox, yet the calendar took it for the middle star of the Ox—
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanhe 2 the Taichu calendar was badly out of step: the sun and moon no longer matched their tabulated positions, and observers agreed that at winter solstice the sun sat at 21° in the Dipper—well short of mid-Ox—though the old system still pretended it was the Ox’s central star

translations.literal: The graph 從 here stands where 後 belongs in the compound 後天 (‘lagging heaven’).
translations.idiomatic: The clause continues in the next line: the calendar ran three quarters of a day behind the sky.

sentences.zh: **[後]*天四分日之三，晦朔弦望差天一日，宿差五度。

translations.literal: —lagging behind heaven by three quarters of a day; last days, new moons, quarters, and full moons differed from heaven by one day, and the lodges differed by five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: —running three quarters of a day slow; conjunctions and phases were one day off, and stellar positions by five degrees.

sentences.zh: 章帝知其謬錯，以問史官，雖知不合，而不能易，故召治歷編欣﹑李梵等綜校其狀[1]。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang knew it was wrong and questioned the clerks; although they knew it did not match, they could not change it, so he summoned the calendar specialists Bian Xin and Li Fan and others to examine and collate the situation comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang saw the error and pressed the astrologers; though they admitted the mismatch, they could not fix it unaided, so he called in Bian Xin, Li Fan, and other calendar specialists for a full review.

sentences.zh: 二月甲寅，遂下詔曰：「朕聞古先聖王，先天而天不違，後天而奉天時。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the jiayin day, he then issued an edict saying: "I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity anticipated heaven and heaven did not oppose them; they followed after heaven and served the seasons of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the second month he promulgated an edict: "The ancient sages moved ahead of heaven without offending it, and when they followed heaven they honored its seasons."

sentences.zh: 河圖曰：『赤九會昌，十世以光，十一以興。

translations.literal: The River Chart says: ‘The Red Nine will meet prosperity; the tenth generation will thereby shine; the eleventh will thereby rise.’
translations.idiomatic: The Hetu says: ‘When the ninth red cycle gathers, ten reigns take their lustre, and the eleventh brings renewal.’"

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『九名之世，帝行德，封刻政。

translations.literal: ’ It also says: ‘In the age of the Nine Names the emperor practices virtue and inscribes his governance on stone.’
translations.idiomatic: It also reads: ‘Under the Nine Names the ruler’s virtue is carved into policy for all to see.’"

sentences.zh: 』朕以不德，奉承大業，夙夜祗畏，不敢荒寧。

translations.literal: ’ I, lacking in virtue, have received the great enterprise; morning and night I am reverent and fearful and dare not be idle or at ease.
translations.idiomatic: With little virtue of my own I have inherited the throne; night and day I hold myself in awe and dare not grow complacent."

sentences.zh: 予末小子，托在於數終，曷以續興，崇弘祖宗，拯濟元元？

translations.literal: I am the least of sons, entrusted at the turning of the cycle—how am I to continue the renewal, exalt the ancestors, and rescue the common people?
translations.idiomatic: I am but the last and least, placed at a cycle’s close—how am I to restore our fortunes, honor our forebears, and bring relief to the people?"

sentences.zh: 尚書琁璣鈐曰：『述堯世，放唐文。

translations.literal: The Shangshu Xuanji qian says: ‘He narrates the age of Yao and releases the pattern of Tang.’
translations.idiomatic: The Classic’s Xuanji qian fragment says: ‘He carries forward Yao’s world and opens Tang’s civilizing pattern.’"

sentences.zh: 』帝命驗曰：『*[順]*堯考德，*

translations.literal: ’ The Diming yan says: ‘He follows Yao and examines virtue—
translations.idiomatic: The Diming yan adds: ‘Align with Yao and weigh virtue—

translations.literal: The graph 顧; some editions read 題 in the following phrase 題期立象.
translations.idiomatic: The line resumes: ‘set the appointed season and fix the cosmic emblems.’

sentences.zh: **[題]*期立象。

translations.literal: —fix the appointed time and establish the images.’
translations.idiomatic: —set the due season and fix the cosmic emblems.’

sentences.zh: 』且三﹑五步驟，優劣殊軌，況乎頑陋，無以克堪，雖欲從之，末由也已。

translations.literal: ’ Moreover, the three- and five-step sequences differ in excellence along separate tracks—how much more I, dull and crude, unable to bear up; though I wish to follow them, there is no way.
translations.idiomatic: Even the triple and quintuple calendrical schemes wander along unequal paths—what hope have I, dull as I am? I long to follow them yet find no footing."

sentences.zh: 每見圖書，中心恧焉。

translations.literal: Whenever I see the charts and writings, my heart is ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever those charts meet my eye I am ashamed at how far we fall short."

sentences.zh: 閒者以來，政治不得，陰陽不和，災異不息，癘疫之氣，流傷於牛，農本不播。

translations.literal: Since recent times governance has not succeeded, yin and yang are not harmonious, prodigies do not cease, pestilential vapors have flowed and harmed the oxen, and the root of agriculture is not sown.
translations.idiomatic: Of late government has faltered, yin and yang fall out of tune, omens pile up, murrain stalks the cattle, and the farmers cannot sow."

sentences.zh: 夫庶征休咎，五事之應，咸在朕躬，信有闕矣，將何以補之？

translations.literal: As for the various omens of weal and woe, the responses of the Five Affairs—all lie in my person; truly there are shortcomings; how shall I remedy them?
translations.idiomatic: The Hong fan warnings attach to the ruler’s conduct; the fault is surely mine—how shall I set it right?"

sentences.zh: 書曰：『惟先假王正厥事。

translations.literal: The Document says: ‘It was when the former kings lent authority that they corrected their affairs.’
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: ‘Ancient kings took heaven’s mandate as their guide and straightened every policy.’"

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『歲二月，東巡狩，至岱宗，柴，望秩於山川。

translations.literal: ’ It also says: ‘In the second month of the year he toured eastward to hunt, arrived at Dai Peak, performed the chai sacrifice, and ranked the sacrifices to mountains and rivers.’
translations.idiomatic: It adds: ‘In the second month he toured east to Mount Tai, offered the great firewood sacrifice, and ordered worship at every peak and stream.’"

sentences.zh: 遂覲東後，□時月正日。

translations.literal: Then he met the lord of the east [lacuna] corrected the seasons, months, and days.
translations.idiomatic: Then, having greeted the guardian of the east, he aligned seasons, months, and days—

sentences.zh: 』祖堯岱宗，同律度量，考在璣衡，以正歷象，庶乎有益。

translations.literal: ’ He honored Yao at Dai Peak, unified pitches and measures, examined matters with the armillary and jade sight-tube, thereby to rectify the calendar and celestial patterns—perhaps there will be benefit.
translations.idiomatic: —like Yao at Mount Tai, harmonizing pitch pipes and weights, checking heaven with the transit instrument until calendar and sky agreed. Perhaps then we may gain something."

sentences.zh: 春秋保干圖曰：『三百年斗歷改憲。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Baogan tu says: ‘After three hundred years the Dipper calendar changes its charter.’
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal Baogan tu declares: ‘Every three hundred years the Dipper-based calendar must be reformed.’"

sentences.zh: 』史官用太初鄧平術，有餘分一，在三百年之域，行度轉差，浸以謬錯。

translations.literal: ’ The clerks use Deng Ping’s Taichu method with a surplus fraction of one; it falls within the three-hundred-year span; the motions turn aside by differences and gradually become erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Our clerks still follow Deng Ping’s Taichu arithmetic—its fractional remainder falls inside the three-hundred-year cycle—yet planetary motion drifts until every degree is wrong."

sentences.zh: 琁璣不正，文象不稽。

translations.literal: The xuanji is not correct; the patterned phenomena are not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The polar sight-line is skewed, so the patterned sky goes unverified."

sentences.zh: 冬至之日日在斗二十*

translations.literal: On the day of the winter solstice the sun is at twenty degrees in the Dipper—
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice the sun stands at twenty—

translations.literal: The marginal gloss (二) completes the compound meaning ‘twenty-one’ with the preceding ‘twenty.’
translations.idiomatic: Read together with the lines before and after, the sun lies at twenty-one Dipper degrees.

sentences.zh: **[一]*度，而歷以為牽牛中星。

translations.literal: —one degree, yet the calendar takes it for the middle star of the Ox.
translations.idiomatic: —one degree in the Dipper, while the calendar still calls it mid-Ox."

sentences.zh: 先立春一日，則四分數之立春日也。

translations.literal: One day before the Beginning of Spring is then the Beginning of Spring day by quarter-day reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: By the quarter-remainder count, ‘Beginning of Spring’ arrives one day ahead of the solar term—

sentences.zh: 以折獄斷大刑，於氣已迕；

translations.literal: —to break lawsuits and decide great punishments by it is already contrary to the qi;
translations.idiomatic: —so trying capital cases by that calendar fights the seasonal qi;

sentences.zh: 用望平和隨時之義，蓋亦遠矣。

translations.literal: to employ the meaning of looking to peace and harmony and following the seasons is surely far off.
translations.idiomatic: and the ideal of tempering justice to the seasons slips ever farther away."

sentences.zh: 今改行四分，以遵於堯，以順孔聖奉天之文。

translations.literal: Now we change and practice the quarter-day system, thereby to accord with Yao and to comply with the pattern by which the Confucian sage serves heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore adopt the quarter-remainder calendar to walk in Yao’s footsteps and heed the model Confucius praised for serving heaven."

sentences.zh: 冀百君子越有民，同心敬授，*[儻]*獲咸*

translations.literal: I hope the hundred nobles, transcending the people, will with one heart reverently grant the seasons—perhaps we may obtain universal—
translations.idiomatic: May every minister join in reverently handing down the seasons—if only we might share in universal—

translations.literal: The graph 喜 glosses the preceding lacuna; commentators prefer the cognate 熙 for the binomial 咸熙 (‘universal radiance’).
translations.idiomatic: Treat this gloss as 熙: universal brightness.

sentences.zh: **[熙]*，以明予祖之遺功。

translations.literal: —splendor—thereby to clarify the surviving merit of my ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: —brightness—and make plain the legacy of my imperial forebears."

sentences.zh: 」於是四分施行。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the quarter-day system was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: With that edict the quarter-remainder calendar entered official use."

sentences.zh: 而欣﹑梵猶以為元首十一月當先大，欲以合耦弦望，命有常日，而十九歲不得七閏，晦朔失實。

translations.literal: But Xin and Fan still held that in the first month of the first year the long month ought to come first, wishing thereby to pair quarters and full moons so that the commands had regular days, yet in nineteen years one did not obtain seven intercalations, and last days and new moons missed reality.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Xin and Li Fan still insisted the civil year should begin with a long eleventh month so quarters and full moons would pair neatly on fixed days—but over nineteen years you still cannot squeeze in seven intercalary months, so conjunctions drifted from fact.

sentences.zh: 行之未期，章帝復發聖思，考之經讖，使左中郎將賈逵問治歷者□承﹑李崇﹑太尉屬梁鮪﹑司徒*[掾]*嚴勖﹑太子舍人徐震﹑鉅鹿公乘蘇統及欣﹑梵等十人。

translations.literal: Before a full cycle of its practice had passed, Emperor Zhang again issued sagely thought, examining it against the classics and prognostications, and sent the General of the Gentlemen of the Household for All Purposes Jia Kui to question the calendar specialists [lacuna] Cheng, Li Chong, the Major to the Grand Commandant Liang Wei, the Clerk of the Minister of Education Yan Xu, the Household Grandee for the Heir Apparent Xu Zhen, the ranked commoner of Julu Su Tong, together with Xin, Fan, and others—ten men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The reform had not run a full term when Emperor Zhang, probing scriptural forecasts anew, commissioned Left General of the Gentlemen Jia Kui to canvass ten experts—including a specialist whose name is damaged in the text, Cheng, Li Chong, Liang Wei the Grand Commandant’s aide, Clerk Yan Xu of the Minister of Education, Heir’s attendant Xu Zhen, Su Tong of Julu, plus Bian Xin and Li Fan.

sentences.zh: 以為月當先小，據春秋經書朔不書晦者，朔必有明晦，不朔必在其月也。

translations.literal: They held that the month ought to have the short month first; according to the Spring and Autumn Annals, when it records new moon it does not record last day—where there is new moon there must be a bright last day; where there is not new moon it must be within that month.
translations.idiomatic: They argued the short month must precede the long: the Annals record first days of months, not month-ends; when the classic gives a conjunction it implies a visible old moon, and if no conjunction is recorded the month still holds together.

sentences.zh: 即先大，則一月再朔，後月無朔，是明不可必。

translations.literal: If one puts the long month first, then one month has two new moons and the following month has no new moon—this brightness is not certain.
translations.idiomatic: Put the long month first and you get two new moons in one month and none in the next—so the lunation cannot hold.

sentences.zh: 梵等以為當先大，無文正驗，取欲諧耦十六日*[望]*，月朓□，晦當滅而已。

translations.literal: Fan and the others held that one ought to put the long month first; there was no textual proof; they merely wished to harmonize pairs on the sixteenth full moon; the moon’s leap [lacuna]; at last day it ought merely to be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan’s party preferred the long month first without textual warrant, merely to align pairs with the fifteenth full moon; they waved away late risings of the moon and treated month-end darkness as enough.

sentences.zh: 又晦與合同時，不得異日。

translations.literal: Moreover last day and conjunction are at the same time and cannot be on different days.
translations.idiomatic: Month-end darkness and true conjunction fall together—they cannot be split across two days.

sentences.zh: 又上知欣﹑梵穴見，□毋拘歷已班，天元始起之月*

translations.literal: Moreover the emperor knew Xin and Fan’s narrow views; [lacuna] do not bind to the calendar already promulgated; the month in which the celestial origin begins—
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also saw how narrow Xin and Fan were; once the published calendar began its epoch, the opening month of heaven’s cycle—

translations.literal: The graph 常 is an alternate manuscript reading for 當 (‘ought to’) in the phrase ‘ought to be short.’
translations.idiomatic: Read this note as 當: the epoch-opening month ought to be short.

translations.literal: —ought to be short.
translations.idiomatic: —must be taken as the short month.

sentences.zh: 定，後年曆數遂正。

translations.literal: Once settled, in later years the calendar numbers were then correct.
translations.idiomatic: Once that ruling stood, the calendar tallies fell into line in the years that followed.

sentences.zh: 永元中，復令史官以九道法候弦望，驗無有差跌。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era, he again ordered the clerks to observe quarters and full moons by the nine-path method, and in verification there were no slips.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongyuan the bureau was told to time quarters and full moons with the nine-path lunar theory; observation showed no misses.

sentences.zh: 逵論集狀，後之議者，用得折衷，故詳錄焉。

translations.literal: Kui’s collected statements on the situation—later debaters used them to strike a middle course; therefore they are recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui’s dossier became the touchstone for later debates, so it is set down here at length.

sentences.zh: 逵論曰：「太初歷冬至日在牽牛初者，牽牛中星也。

translations.literal: Kui stated in discussion: "In the Taichu calendar the winter solstice sun at the beginning of the Ox is the middle star of the Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui argued: "The Taichu calendar places winter solstice at the Ox’s leading edge and calls that ‘mid-Ox.’"

sentences.zh: 古黃帝﹑夏﹑殷﹑周﹑魯冬至日在建星，建星即今斗星也。

translations.literal: For ancient Huang Di, Xia, Yin, Zhou, and Lu the winter solstice sun was at Establishment Star; Establishment Star is today’s Dipper star.
translations.idiomatic: The classical calendars of Huang Di, Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Lu put winter solstice at Establishment Star—which is our Dipper asterism."

sentences.zh: 太初歷斗二十六度三百八十五分，牽牛八度。

translations.literal: The Taichu calendar has the Dipper at twenty-six degrees three hundred eighty-five parts and the Ox at eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu assigns twenty-six degrees plus 385 fractional parts to the Dipper and eight degrees to the Ox."

sentences.zh: 案行事史官注，冬﹑夏至日常不及太初歷五度，冬至日在斗*

translations.literal: Examining the practicing clerks’ annotations, winter and summer solstice days regularly fell short of the Taichu calendar by five degrees; the winter solstice sun was in the Dipper—
translations.idiomatic: Working registers show solstice positions consistently five degrees shy of Taichu; at winter solstice the sun stood in the Dipper—

sentences.zh: 尚書考靈曜『斗二十二度，無餘分，冬至在牽牛所起』。

sentences.zh: 又編欣等據今日所在*[未至]*牽牛中星五度，於斗二十一度四分一，與考靈曜相近，即以明事。

translations.literal: Moreover Bian Xin and others based themselves on today’s location not yet reaching five degrees to the middle star of the Ox, being at twenty-one and one-quarter degrees in the Dipper, close to the Kaoling yao, thereby clarifying the matter.

sentences.zh: 元和二年八月，詔書曰『石不可離』，令兩候，上得筭多者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second Yuanhe year, an edict said ‘Stone cannot be separated,’ ordering two observers; whoever obtained more on the counting-rods went up.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 2, month 8, an edict declared ‘the benchmark must not be split,’ pitting two observing teams—the one with superior rod reckonings prevailed."

translations.literal: Therefore in seeking degrees and numbers, taking accordance with sun, moon, and asterisms, there are techniques of different ages.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking degree measures that fit sun, moon, and stars has always meant borrowing methods suited to different eras.

sentences.zh: 太初歷不能下通於今，新歷不能上得漢元。

translations.literal: The Taichu calendar cannot extend downward to the present; the new calendar cannot reach upward to Han’s inception.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu cannot be stretched intact to today’s sky; the new system cannot be wound backward to Han’s founding year.

sentences.zh: 一家曆法必在三百年之閒。

translations.literal: A single family’s calendar method must lie within three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Any one calendrical school stays reliable only within about three centuries.

sentences.zh: 故讖文曰『三百年斗歷改憲』。

translations.literal: Therefore the prognostication text says, ‘After three hundred years the Dipper calendar changes its charter.’
translations.idiomatic: Hence the apocryphon: ‘After three hundred years reform the Dipper-based calendar.’"

sentences.zh: 漢興，當用太初而不改，下至太初元年百二歲乃改。

translations.literal: When Han rose, it ought to have used Taichu but did not change; down to the first year of Taichu, after one hundred two years, it then changed.
translations.idiomatic: At Han’s rise Taichu should have been adopted at once; instead the reform waited until Taichu year 1—one hundred two years later.

sentences.zh: 故其前有先晦一日合朔，下至成﹑哀，以二日為朔，故合朔多在晦，此其明效也。」

translations.literal: Therefore before that there was conjunction one day before last day; down to Cheng and Ai they took two days for new moon, so conjunctions mostly fell on last days—this is its clear effect."
translations.idiomatic: Early Han conjunctions came a day before month-end; by Cheng and Ai people counted two-day lunations, so true conjunctions clustered on month-ends—the clearest proof of drift."

sentences.zh: 逵論曰：「臣前上傅安等用黃道度日月弦望多近。

translations.literal: Kui stated in discussion: "Your servant previously submitted that Fu An and others used the yellow path to measure sun and moon; quarters and full moons were mostly close.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui continued: "I once reported that Fu An’s team measured sun and moon along the ecliptic and matched quarters and full moons far better."

sentences.zh: 史官一以赤道度之，不與日月同，於今歷弦望至差一日以上，輒奏以為變，至以為日□縮退行。

translations.literal: The clerks uniformly measured them by the red path; they did not agree with sun and moon; with today’s calendar quarters and full moons miss by more than one day; they then memorialize deeming it a prodigy, even deeming the sun’s shrinkage and retreating motion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bureau insists on equatorial coordinates, which diverge from the bodies’ true paths: quarters and full moons slip by a full day, so clerks cry anomaly—or even claim the sun is shrinking and retreating—

sentences.zh: 於黃道，自得行度，不為變。

translations.literal: With respect to the yellow path, they obtain their own motions of travel and it is not a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: —whereas on the ecliptic the motions are steady and nothing ominous occurs."

sentences.zh: 願請太史官日月宿簿及星度課，與待詔星象考校。

translations.literal: I wish to request the Grand Astrologer’s sun and moon lodge registers and star-degree reckonings, and to examine and collate them with the expectancy-holders for asterisms.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to compare the Grand Astrologer’s solar and lunar lodge logs—along with every star-degree computation—with the expectancy-holders who chart constellations."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the request."

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：前對言冬至日去極一百一十五度，夏至日去極六十七度，春秋分日去極九十一度。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: in the previous reply it was said that on the winter solstice day the distance from the pole is one hundred fifteen degrees; on the summer solstice day sixty-seven degrees; on the spring and autumn equinox days ninety-one degrees.
translations.idiomatic: As I reported earlier: winter solstice lies 115° from the pole, summer solstice 67°, and the equinoxes 91°."

sentences.zh: 洪範『日月之行，則有冬夏』。

translations.literal: The Hong fan [says]: ‘In the travels of sun and moon there are winter and summer.’
translations.idiomatic: The Hong fan teaches that the sun and moon trace winter and summer arcs—"

sentences.zh: 五紀論『日月循黃道，南至牽牛，北至東井，率日日行一度，月行十三度十九分度七』也。

translations.literal: The Wuji lun [says]: ‘Sun and moon follow the yellow path; south they reach the Ox, north they reach Eastern Well; as a rule the sun travels one degree per day, the moon thirteen and seven-nineteenths degrees per day.’
translations.idiomatic: —and the Wuji lun adds that both bodies ride the ecliptic between Ox and Eastern Well, the sun about one degree per day and the moon thirteen and seven nineteenths."

sentences.zh: 今史官一以赤道為度，不與日月行同，其斗﹑牽牛﹑*[東井]*﹑輿鬼，赤道得十五，而黃道得十三度半；

translations.literal: Now the clerks uniformly take the red path as degrees; they do not agree with the travels of sun and moon; for the Dipper, Ox, Eastern Well, and Ghosts, the red path obtains fifteen, while the yellow path obtains thirteen and a half degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Today’s clerks measure everything on the celestial equator, not along the true paths: for the Dipper, Ox, Eastern Well, and Ghosts the equator spans fifteen degrees while the ecliptic needs only thirteen and a half—

sentences.zh: 行東壁﹑奎﹑婁﹑軫﹑角﹑亢，赤道*

translations.literal: traveling Eastern Wall, Legs, Bond, Chariot-Frame, Horn, and Neck, the red path—
translations.idiomatic: —crossing Eastern Wall, Legs, Bond, Chariot-Frame, Horn, and Neck the equator records—

translations.literal: The transmitted graph 十 completes seventeen degrees together with the preceding seven.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the preceding line this yields seventeen equatorial degrees versus eight on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: **[七]*度，黃道八度；

translations.literal: —seventeen degrees, the yellow path eight degrees;
translations.idiomatic: —seventeen degrees while the ecliptic shows eight—

sentences.zh: 或月行多而日月相去反少，謂之日□。

translations.literal: or the moon’s travel is much yet the sun and moon’s mutual distance is instead small—this is called the sun’s [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: —so sometimes the moon moves far yet looks close to the sun, which clerks mislabel as solar ‘shortening.’"

sentences.zh: 案黃道值牽牛，出赤道南二十五度，其直東井﹑輿鬼，出赤道北*[二十]*五度。

translations.literal: Examining the yellow path when it meets the Ox, it emerges twenty-five degrees south of the red path; where it is straight with Eastern Well and Ghosts, it emerges twenty-five degrees north of the red path.
translations.idiomatic: Where the ecliptic crosses the Ox it sits twenty-five degrees south of the equator; opposite Eastern Well and Ghosts it lies twenty-five degrees north—

sentences.zh: 赤道者為中天，去極俱九十度，非日月道，而以遙准度日月，失其實行故也。

translations.literal: The red path is taken as middle heaven; from the pole it is uniformly ninety degrees; it is not the path of sun and moon, yet by remote reckoning they measure sun and moon—thereby missing their true motions.
translations.idiomatic: The equator marks mid-sky at ninety degrees from the pole, but it is not where the luminaries travel; gauging them by that circle misses their real paths.

sentences.zh: 以今太史官候注考元和二年九月已來月行牽牛﹑東井四十九事，無行十一度者；

translations.literal: Taking the present Grand Astrologer’s observation annotations and examining forty-nine instances since the ninth month of Yuanhe 2 of the moon traveling Ox and Eastern Well, there was none that traveled eleven degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanhe 2, month 9, the bureau logged forty-nine lunar passages through Ox and Eastern Well—not once did the moon move eleven degrees along the equator.

sentences.zh: 行婁﹑角三十七事，無行十五六度者，如安言。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven instances traveling Bond and Horn—there was none that traveled fifteen or sixteen degrees—just as An said.
translations.idiomatic: Across thirty-seven passages near Bond and Horn there were no fifteen- or sixteen-degree equatorial arcs, exactly as Fu An claimed.

sentences.zh: 問典星待詔姚崇﹑井畢等十二人，皆曰『星圖有規法，日月實從黃道，官無其器，不知施行』。

translations.literal: Twelve men including the expectancy-holders for canon stars Yao Chong and Jing Bi were questioned; they all said, ‘Star charts have compass rules; sun and moon truly follow the yellow path; the office lacks its instruments and does not know how to implement it.’
translations.idiomatic: Twelve star-chart specialists including Yao Chong and Jing Bi were polled; each admitted that charts follow compass geometry, that sun and moon ride the ecliptic, and that without proper instruments the bureau could not put the theory into practice.

sentences.zh: 案甘露二年大司農中丞耿壽昌奏，以圖儀度日月行，考驗天運狀，日月行至牽牛﹑東井，日過*[一]*度，月行十五度，至婁﹑角，日行一度，月行十三度，赤道使然，此前世所共知也。

translations.literal: Examining the memorial of the second Ganlu year by Palace Assistant to the Minister of Agriculture Geng Shouchang, using diagram instruments to measure sun and moon motion and verify the pattern of heaven’s circuit: when sun and moon reach Ox and Eastern Well, the sun exceeds one degree and the moon fifteen degrees; when they reach Bond and Horn, the sun travels one degree per day and the moon thirteen—the red path causes this; this was commonly known in earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Shouchang’s Ganlu 2 memorial already used armillary diagrams to track the luminaries: near Ox and Eastern Well the sun gains more than a degree daily and the moon about fifteen; near Bond and Horn the solar rate is one degree and the lunar thirteen—effects of measuring on the equator, as earlier ages understood.

sentences.zh: 如言黃道有驗，合天，日無前□，弦望不差一日，比用赤道密近，宜施用。

translations.literal: If one says the yellow path has verification, matches heaven, the sun has no prior slackening, quarters and full moons miss by not one day—compared with using the red path it is dense and close; it ought to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: If the ecliptic checks out against the sky—no spurious solar slowdown and quarters within a day—the method beats equatorial reckoning and deserves adoption.

sentences.zh: 上中多臣校。

translations.literal: What went up matched much of your servant’s comparisons.
translations.idiomatic: The throne’s findings matched most of my cross-checks.

sentences.zh: 」案逵論，永元四年也。

translations.literal: ” Examining Kui’s discussion, it was the fourth Yongyuan year.
translations.idiomatic: This concludes Jia Kui’s memorial from Yongyuan 4.

sentences.zh: 至十五年七月甲辰，詔書造太史黃道銅儀，以角為十三度，亢十，氐十六，房五，心五，尾十八，箕十，斗二十四四分度之一，牽牛七，須女十一，虛十，危十六，營室十八，東壁十，奎十七，婁十二，胃十五，昴十二，畢十六，觜三，參八，東井三十，輿鬼四，柳十四，星七，張十七，翼十九，軫十八，凡三百六十五度四分度之一。

sentences.zh: 冬至日在斗十九度四分度之一。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice the sun was at nineteen and one-quarter degrees in the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice was fixed at 19¼° in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 史官以*

translations.idiomatic: The clerks classified—

translations.idiomatic: Scribes wrote 郭 where 部 (‘division’) belongs.

translations.literal: —‘division’—sun and moon motions, referencing quarters and full moons; although dense and close, they did not annotate the days.
translations.idiomatic: They paired solar and lunar motions by lodge divisions with quarters and full moons; though numerically tight, they never tied those arcs to specific calendar days.

sentences.zh: 儀，黃道與度轉運，難以候，是以少循其事。

translations.literal: As for the instrument, the yellow path and degrees revolve and shift—difficult to observe—therefore they seldom followed through on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Because the ecliptic ring and degree circle spin together, observations were awkward and the bureau rarely followed the procedure.

sentences.zh: 逵論曰：「又今史官推合朔、弦、望、月食加時，率多不中，在於不知月行□疾意。

translations.literal: Kui stated in discussion: “Moreover, today’s clerks in computing conjunction, quarters, full moons, and lunar-eclipse times mostly miss, because they do not know the import of the moon’s fast and slow motion.”
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui added: “The bureau still mis-times conjunctions, quarters, full moons, and eclipses because it does not grasp how the moon speeds up and slows down.”

sentences.zh: 永平中，詔書令故太史待詔張隆以四分法署弦、望、月食加時。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era, an edict ordered the former Grand Astrologer’s expectancy-holder Zhang Long to use the quarter-day method to determine quarters, full moons, and lunar-eclipse times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongping the emperor told former expectancy-holder Zhang Long to set quarters, full moons, and eclipse times with the quarter-remainder system.

sentences.zh: 隆言能用易九、六、七、八*

translations.literal: Long said he could use the Changes’ nine, six, seven, eight—
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Long claimed he could read the moon’s range from the Classic’s nine, six, seven, eight lines—

translations.literal: —‘yao lines’—to know how much the moon travels.
translations.idiomatic: —using the hexagram lines—to gauge how far the moon moves each night.

sentences.zh: 今案隆所署多失。

translations.literal: Now examining Long’s determinations, many missed.
translations.idiomatic: Review shows Zhang Long’s predictions were usually wrong.

sentences.zh: 臣使隆逆推前手所署，不應，或異日，不中天乃益遠，至十餘度。

translations.literal: Your servant had Long reverse-extrapolate what his predecessors had determined; they did not match, or were on different days; missing mid-heaven became still farther—up to more than ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: I had him back-calculate earlier postings: they failed to match, sometimes fell on the wrong day, and missed transit by more than ten degrees.

sentences.zh: 梵、統以史官候注考校，月行當有□疾，不必在牽牛、東井、婁、角之閒，又非所謂朓、側匿，乃由月所行道有遠近出入所生，率一月移故所疾處三度，九歲九道一復，凡九章，百七十一歲，復十一月合朔旦冬至，合春秋、三統九道終數，可以知合朔、弦、望、月食加時。

translations.literal: Fan and Tong compared against the clerks’ observation annotations: the moon’s motion ought to have fast and slow phases; it need not lie between Ox, Eastern Well, Bond, and Horn, nor is it what is called ‘late rising’ or ‘lateral hiding’—it arises from the road the moon travels having far and near, exit and entry; on average in one month the former fast place shifts three degrees; in nine years the nine paths complete one cycle; in all nine chapters, at one hundred seventy-one years, one returns to eleventh-month conjunction at dawn on the winter solstice, matching the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Triple Concordance nine-path terminal numbers—thereby one can know conjunction, quarters, full moons, and lunar-eclipse times.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan and Su Tong checked the observation logs: lunar speed varies; the extremes need not occur only near Ox, Eastern Well, Bond, or Horn, nor are they mere ‘late first quarters’ or hidden crescents—they come from the moon’s varying distance along its path, drifting about three degrees per month in the sector of fastest motion. Nine years recycle the nine paths; after nine cycles and 171 years you realign an eleventh-month winter-solstice conjunction, matching the Spring and Autumn annals and Triple Concordance nine-path periods—enough to pin conjunctions, quarters, full moons, and eclipses.

sentences.zh: 據官注天度為分率，以其術法上考建武以來月食凡三十八事，差密近，有益，*

translations.literal: Taking the official annotations’ celestial degrees as fractional rates, and with his technique examining upward thirty-eight lunar-eclipse cases since Jianwu, the differences are dense and close—there is benefit—
translations.idiomatic: Using bureau degree logs as denominators, his method retrodicts thirty-eight eclipses since Jianwu with tight agreement—clear gains—

translations.literal: The graph 宣 is a manuscript miswriting for 宜.
translations.idiomatic: Read this gloss as 宜 ‘ought to.’

translations.literal: —‘ought’—to test it at court.”
translations.idiomatic: —so it ought to be tried before the throne.”

sentences.zh: 案史官舊有九道術，廢而不修。

translations.literal: Examining the clerks: they formerly had the nine-path method; it was abandoned and not cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau once maintained the nine-path lunar theory but let it lapse.

sentences.zh: 熹平中，故治歷郎梁國宗整上九道術，詔書下太史，以參舊術，相應。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era, the former Director of Calendars Zong Zheng of Liang kingdom submitted the nine-path method; an edict sent it down to the Grand Astrologer to compare with the old method—it corresponded.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiping, former calendar director Zong Zheng of Liang resubmitted the nine-path theory; the throne ordered the Grand Astrologer to cross-check it against older tables and the results aligned.

sentences.zh: 部太子舍人馮恂課校，恂亦復作九道術，增損其分，與整術並校，差為近。

translations.literal: The division Supernumerary of the Heir Apparent Feng Xun examined and collated; Xun also again composed a nine-path method, increasing or decreasing its fractions, and collated it alongside Zheng’s method—the differences were comparatively close.
translations.idiomatic: Heir-apparent attendant Feng Xun reviewed both versions, drafted his own nine-path adjustments, and compared them with Zong Zheng’s—the discrepancies shrank.

sentences.zh: 太史令揚上以恂術參弦、望。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Yang Shang used Xun’s method to aid quarters and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Yang blended Feng Xun’s tables into quarter- and full-moon predictions.

sentences.zh: 然而加時猶復先後天，遠則十餘度[2]。

translations.literal: Yet in adding the times they still were early or late relative to heaven; at far extremes more than ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Even then predicted moments still ran ahead or behind the sky—sometimes by more than ten degrees.

sentences.zh: 永元十四年，待詔太史霍融上言：「官漏刻率九日增減一刻，不與天相應，或時差至二刻半，不如夏歷密。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth Yongyuan year, expectancy-holder Grand Astrologer Huo Rong submitted a memorial saying: ‘The official clepsydra on average every nine days adds or subtracts one mark; it does not match heaven; sometimes the discrepancy reaches two and a half marks; it is not as dense as the Xia calendar.’
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 14, expectancy Huo Rong reported that the bureau water-clock drifted a notch every nine days out of step with the sky—sometimes by two and a half notches—and fell short of the Xia calendar’s precision.

sentences.zh: 」詔書下太常，令史官與融以儀校天，課度遠近。

translations.literal: ’ An edict went down to the Grand Master of Ceremonies ordering the clerks together with Rong to use instruments to verify heaven and reckon distances far and near.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to have the bureau join Huo Rong in checking the sky with instruments and measuring solar distance.

sentences.zh: 太史令舒、承、梵等對：「案官所施漏法令甲第六常符漏品，孝宣皇帝三年十二月乙酉下，建武十年二月壬午詔書施行。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologers Shu, Cheng, Fan, and others replied: ‘Examining the clepsydra statute applied by the office—section six of the ordinances on perpetual tally clepsydras—issued on yiyou in the twelfth month of the third year of Emperor Xuan, implemented by edict on renwu in the second month of the tenth Jianwu year.’
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologers Shu, Cheng, and Fan answered that the clepsydra rules came from statute bundle A, section six—promulgated under Emperor Xuan and reaffirmed in Jianwu 10.

sentences.zh: 漏刻以日長短為數，率日南北二度四分而增減一刻。

translations.literal: Clepsydra marks take day length as their number; as a rule for each two and four-tenths degrees south or north of the sun one adds or subtracts one mark.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra scaling tracks seasonal day length: each 2.4° shift of the sun toward north or south adjusts the water-clock by one mark.

sentences.zh: 一氣俱十五日，日去極各有多少。

translations.literal: Each qi-period alike is fifteen days; the sun’s distance from the pole each has more or less.
translations.idiomatic: Every fortnightly period spans fifteen days, and the sun’s polar distance changes within it.

sentences.zh: 今官漏率九日移一刻，不隨日進退。

translations.literal: Now the official clepsydra on average every nine days shifts one mark; it does not follow the sun’s advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s clock advances one notch every nine days regardless of how the sun moves—a mismatch.

sentences.zh: 夏歷漏*[刻]*隨日南北為長短，密近於官漏，分明可施行。

translations.literal: The Xia calendar’s clepsydra marks follow the sun south and north as long and short; they are dense and close to the official clepsydra; clearly they can be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia-style clepsydra lengthens and shortens with the sun’s seasonal swing; it tracks the official clock closely enough to deploy.

sentences.zh: 」其年十一月甲寅，詔曰：「告司徒、司空：漏所以節時分，定□明。

translations.literal: ’ In that year’s eleventh month on jiayin day an edict said: ‘Inform the Ministers of Education and Works: the clepsydra is what regulates seasonal divisions and fixes day and night clarity.’
translations.idiomatic: That year on jiayin in month 11 an edict told the Ministers of Education and Works that clepsydras govern seasonal divisions and fix daylight hours.

sentences.zh: □明長短，起於日去極遠近，日道周*[圜]*，不可以計率分，當據儀度，下參晷景。

translations.literal: The length and shortness of day and night clarity rise from the sun’s distance from the far and near; the sun’s path is circular; one cannot by computed rates divide it; one ought to rely on instrument measures and below reference gnomon shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Day length depends on how far the sun stands from the pole; the solar path is a great circle, so you cannot simply average it—set the clepsydra from armillary measures and gnomon readings.

sentences.zh: 今官漏以計率分□明，九日增減一刻，違失其實，至為疏數以耦法。

translations.literal: Now the official clepsydra by computed rates divides day and night light; every nine days it adds or subtracts one mark—violating the reality, even to being coarse in number in order to pair the method.
translations.idiomatic: The present clock forces daylight into crude nine-day steps—wrong in fact and artificially averaged just to keep arithmetic tidy.

sentences.zh: 太史待詔霍融上言，不與天相應。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer expectancy-holder Huo Rong submitted a memorial saying it does not match heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Expectancy Huo Rong showed it fails against the sky.

sentences.zh: 太常史官運儀下水，官漏失天者至三刻。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies clerks operated instruments and poured water; where the official clepsydra missed heaven reached three marks.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry ran trials against instruments, the palace clepsydra could miss true time by three marks.

sentences.zh: 以晷景為刻，少所違失，密近有驗。

translations.literal: Taking gnomon shadow as marks, there is little deviation; dense and close with verification.
translations.idiomatic: Basing notches on sundial shadows stays closer to observation with fewer errors.

sentences.zh: 今下晷景漏刻四十八箭，立成斧官府當用者，計吏到，班予四十八箭。

translations.literal: Now distributing forty-eight clepsydra arrow-tubes of gnomon shadow marks, standing completion axes—what offices ought to use—when accounting clerks arrive, distribute to them the forty-eight arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Issue the forty-eight seasonal tube-settings derived from gnomon shadows; give copies to every department when fiscal clerks arrive.

sentences.zh: 」文多，故魁取二十四氣日所在，並黃道去極、晷景、漏刻、□明中星刻於下。

translations.literal: ’ The text is abundant; therefore only selecting where the twenty-four qi-days reside, together with yellow-path distance from pole, gnomon shadow, clepsydra marks, and mid-heaven asterisms at day and night clarity—are inscribed below.
translations.idiomatic: Because the full text is long, the excerpt below lists only each qi-day’s solar longitude, ecliptic polar distance, shadow length, clepsydra setting, day-night ratio, and culminating star.

sentences.zh: 昔太初歷之興也，發謀於元封，啟定於*

translations.literal: Formerly when the Taichu calendar arose, planning began in Yuanfeng, fixing opened at—
translations.idiomatic: The Taichu reform was planned under Yuanfeng and settled when—

translations.literal: The graph 天 is an error for 元 in the reign name Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Correct the character to 元: the reform was confirmed in Yuanfeng.

translations.literal: —‘Yuan’—Feng—accumulating—
translations.idiomatic: —the Yuanfeng era—after thirty years—

translations.literal: The graph 百 is an erroneous duplication and should be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Drop the stray 百 before 三十年.

sentences.zh: *三十年，是非乃審。

translations.literal: —thirty years—then right and wrong were examined.
translations.idiomatic: —thirty years—the verdict on Taichu finally settled.

sentences.zh: 及用四分，亦於建武，施於元和，訖於永元，七十餘年，然後儀式備立，司候有准。

translations.literal: By the time the quarter-day system was used, likewise beginning at Jianwu, implemented at Yuanhe, ending at Yongyuan—more than seventy years—then models and forms were fully established and observers had standards.
translations.idiomatic: The quarter-remainder calendar launched under Guangwu, took effect in Yuanhe, and stabilized through Yongyuan—only after seventy years did instruments and observing protocols settle.

sentences.zh: 天事幽微，若此其難也。

translations.literal: Heavenly affairs are subtle and hidden—thus difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Even celestial mathematics proves this subtle and painstaking.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，圖讖漏洩，而考靈曜、命歷序皆有甲寅元。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, charts and prognostications have leaked out, and both Kaoling yao and Mingli xu have jiayin-yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Since Guangwu’s revival, apocrypha have circulated openly; Kaoling yao and Mingli xu both advocate the jiayin epoch.

sentences.zh: 其所起在四分庚申元後百一十四歲，朔差□二日。

translations.literal: Its starting lies one hundred fourteen years after the quarter-day gengshen yuan; conjunction misses two days [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: That epoch begins 114 years after the quarter system’s gengshen origin and differs by about two days on mean lunations.

sentences.zh: 學士修之於草澤，信向以為得正。

translations.literal: Scholars cultivated it in the marshes and trusted it as obtaining correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Rustic scholars tinkered with it in exile and convinced themselves they had the true calendar.

sentences.zh: 及太初歷以後*

translations.literal: When after the Taichu calendar—
translations.idiomatic: Advocates of Taichu argue heaven runs fast—

translations.literal: The graph 大 is an error for 天.
translations.idiomatic: Read 天 to yield ‘heaven is fast.’

sentences.zh: **[天]*為疾，而修之者云「百四十四歲而太歲超一*

translations.literal: —‘heaven’—is fast, and those who cultivate it say, ‘In one hundred forty-four years the Grand Year leaps one—
translations.idiomatic: —they say heaven runs ahead and that every 144 years the Jupiter cycle skips one—

translations.literal: The graph 表 is an error for 辰.
translations.idiomatic: Read 辰: Jupiter skips one celestial stem.

sentences.zh: **[辰]*，百七十一歲當棄朔余六十三，中余千一百九十七，乃可常行」。

translations.literal: —‘chen’—in one hundred seventy-one years one ought to discard conjunction remainder sixty-three and middle remainder one thousand one hundred ninety-seven—then it can constantly proceed.’
translations.idiomatic: —hour-branch—after 171 years discard 63 from the lunation fraction and 1197 from the middle qi remainder—only then can the cycle run smoothly.’

sentences.zh: 自太初元年至永平十一年，百七十一，當去分而不去，故令益有疏闊。

translations.literal: From the first Taichu year to the eleventh Yongping year—one hundred seventy-one—one ought to discard fractions but did not discard them; therefore it caused increasing looseness.
translations.idiomatic: Between Taichu 1 and Yongping 11 lies one full 171-year cycle where the prescribed remainder should have been dropped but was not, so the calendar drifted further.

sentences.zh: 此二家常挾其術，庶幾施行，每有訟者，百寮會議，腢儒騁思，論之有方，益於多聞識之，故詳錄焉。

translations.literal: These two houses constantly harbor their techniques, hoping almost to implement them; whenever there are disputants, the hundred offices convene in conference; Confucians across the realm unleash thought; discussing it has method—beneficial for broad hearing and knowing—therefore it is recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Both schools cling to their arithmetic and lobby for adoption; whenever debate arises the court convenes scholars whose arguments repay study—hence the full record here.

sentences.zh: 安帝延光二年，中謁者但誦言當用甲寅元，河南梁豐言當復用太初。

translations.literal: In the second Yanguang year of Emperor An, the Palace Intern Dan Song said one ought to use the jiayin yuan; Liang Feng of Henan said one ought to restore using Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanguang 2, intern Dan Song urged the jiayin epoch while Henan’s Liang Feng called for a return to Taichu.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎張衡、周興皆能歷，數難誦、豐，或不對，或言失誤。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Zhang Heng and Zhou Xing were both capable in calendrics; they repeatedly challenged Song and Feng—sometimes they did not answer, sometimes their words were mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng and Zhou Xing, both skilled in astronomy, cross-examined Dan Song and Liang Feng, who either fell silent or misspoke.

sentences.zh: 衡、興參案儀注*

translations.literal: Heng and Xing examined and collated the instrument regulations—
translations.idiomatic: They collated the armillary regulations—

translations.literal: The graph 者 is a superfluous particle.
translations.idiomatic: Omit the stray character 者.

sentences.zh: *，考往校今，以為九道法最密。

translations.literal: —examining past and comparing present—they deemed the nine-path method densest.
translations.idiomatic: —then tested past records against the sky—and judged the nine-path theory tightest.

sentences.zh: 詔書下公卿詳議。

translations.literal: An edict went down ordering dukes and ministers to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the high ministers to debate the proposals.

sentences.zh: 太尉愷等上侍中施延等議：「太初過天，日一度，弦望失正，月以晦見西方，食不與天相應；

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Kai and others presented Palace Attendant Shi Yan’s party’s discussion: ‘Taichu exceeds heaven by one degree per day; quarters and full moons lose correctness; the moon is seen in the west at last day; eclipses do not match heaven.’
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Kai relayed Shi Yan’s faction: Taichu runs one solar degree ahead daily, corrupts lunations, lets the moon appear in the west at month-end, and misstates eclipses.

sentences.zh: 元和改從四分，四分雖密於太初，復不正，皆不可用。

translations.literal: Yuanhe changed to follow the quarter-day system; although the quarter-day is denser than Taichu, again it is not correct—both are unusable.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanhe reform adopted quarter-remainder math—better than Taichu yet still flawed—so neither scheme suffices.

sentences.zh: 甲寅元與天相應，合圖讖，可施行。」

translations.literal: The jiayin yuan matches heaven and agrees with charts and prognostications—it can be implemented.’
translations.idiomatic: Only the jiayin epoch tracks heaven and matches the apocrypha—it should be adopted.’

sentences.zh: 博士黃廣、大行令任僉議，如九道。

translations.literal: Erudite Huang Guang and Chief Clerk for Grand Processions Ren Qian discussed—like the nine-path.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guang and Ren Qian sided with the nine-path lunar scheme.

sentences.zh: 河南尹祉、太子舍人李泓等四十人議：「即用甲寅元，當除元命苞天地開闢獲麟中百一十四歲，推閏月六直其日，或朔、晦、弦、望，二十四氣宿度不相應者非一。

translations.literal: Henan Governor Zhi, Heir-apparent Supernumerary Li Hong, and forty others discussed: ‘If one immediately uses the jiayin yuan, one must eliminate one hundred fourteen years within the Yuanming bao’s Heaven-Earth opening and unicorn capture; intercalary months pushed six straight to their days—or new moon, last day, quarters, full moons—cases where the twenty-four qi-lodge degrees do not correspond are not one.’
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhi of Henan and forty colleagues warned that adopting jiayin would delete 114 years from the Yuanming bao chronology, scramble intercalations, and leave many mismatches among conjunctions, phases, and solar lodge positions.

sentences.zh: 用九道為朔，月有比三大二小，皆疏遠。

translations.literal: Using the nine-path as new moon, months have repeated patterns of three large and two small—all are loose and distant.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-path lunations produce awkward strings of three long and two short months—too unwieldy.

sentences.zh: 元和變曆，以應保干圖『三百歲斗歷改憲』之文。

translations.literal: Yuanhe altered the calendar to respond to the Baogan tu’s text ‘after three hundred years the Dipper calendar changes its charter.’
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang’s Yuanhe reform invoked the Baogan tu promise of changing the Dipper calendar every three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 四分歷本起圖讖，最得其正，不宜易。

translations.literal: The quarter-day calendar fundamentally arose from charts and prognostications; it most obtains its correctness; it is not appropriate to change.
translations.idiomatic: The quarter system springs from canonical forecasts and already hits the mark—it should not be tossed aside.

sentences.zh: 」愷等八十四人議，宜從太初。

translations.literal: ’ Kai and eighty-four others discussed—one ought to follow Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai and eighty-four scholars urged sticking with Taichu.

sentences.zh: 尚書令忠上奏：「諸從太初者，皆無他效驗，徒以世宗攘夷廓境，享國久長為辭。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Director Zhong submitted a memorial: ‘Those who follow Taichu all lack other verification; they merely take as rhetoric Shizong’s repelling barbarians and expanding borders, enjoying the state long.’
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhong Chen argued that Taichu’s defenders cite only Emperor Wu’s military glory and long reign—no astronomical proof.

sentences.zh: 或云孝章改四分，災異卒甚，未有善應。

translations.literal: Some say Emperor Zhang changed to quarter-day—prodigies ended severely—there was no good response.
translations.idiomatic: Others blame Emperor Zhang’s quarter reform for a rash of omens—yet saw no blessing.

sentences.zh: 臣伏惟聖王興起，各異正朔，以通三統。

translations.literal: Your servant bows and considers: sagely kings rising each differ correct beginnings to penetrate the three ties.
translations.idiomatic: Each sage founder adopts his own calendar stance to complete the triple succession.

sentences.zh: 漢祖受命，因秦之紀，十月為年首，閏常在歲後。

translations.literal: Han’s ancestor received the mandate, taking Qin’s reckoning—the tenth month as year head—intercalations constantly after the year.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu inherited Qin’s calendar—year beginning in the tenth month—always tucking intercalations after year-end.

sentences.zh: 不稽先代，違於帝典。

translations.literal: Not examining former ages—contrary to the Emperor’s canon.
translations.idiomatic: That ignored antiquity and offended the classical canon.

sentences.zh: 太宗遵修，三階以平，黃龍以至，刑犴以錯，五者以備[3]。

translations.literal: Taizong followed and cultivated—the three ranks thereby level; yellow dragons thereby arrived; punishments and prisons thereby aligned—the five thereby complete.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen restored proper seasons so harmony returned—omens aligned, justice balanced, and the Hong fan ‘five affairs’ fell into place.

sentences.zh: 哀平之際，同承太初，而妖孽累仍，痾禍非一。

translations.literal: At the juncture of Ai and Ping, alike inheriting Taichu—yet prodigies piled up repeatedly; sickness and calamity were not one.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ai and Ping everyone still used Taichu—yet omens and disasters multiplied.

sentences.zh: 議者不以成數相參，考真求實，而泛采妄說，歸福太初，致咎四分。

translations.literal: Discussants do not use completed numbers to cross-reference, examining truth and seeking substance—rather they broadly gather reckless doctrines, attributing blessing to Taichu and assigning blame to quarter-day.
translations.idiomatic: Critics cherry-pick omens instead of testing arithmetic: they credit Taichu for every blessing and blame every ill on the quarter reform.

sentences.zh: 太初歷觿賢所立，是非已定，永平不審，復革其弦望。

translations.literal: Taichu calendar—worthy men established it—right and wrong already settled; Yongping did not examine carefully and again altered its quarters and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu was fixed by experts; Yongping meddled again with lunations without understanding.

sentences.zh: 四分有謬，不可施行。

translations.literal: The quarter-day has error—it cannot be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The quarter scheme remains flawed and must not replace Taichu wholesale.

sentences.zh: 元和鳳鳥不當應歷而翔集。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe phoenix birds ought not respond to the calendar yet soar and gather.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanhe phoenix omens did not match what the quarter calendar predicted.

sentences.zh: 遠嘉前造，則*

translations.literal: Praising afar the earlier creation, then—
translations.idiomatic: Praising distant antiquity—

translations.literal: The graph 喪 is an error for 表.
translations.idiomatic: Read 表 ‘display’ rather than 喪.

translations.literal: —‘display’—its flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: —they trumpet ancient blessings;

sentences.zh: 近譏後改，則隱其福。

translations.literal: Near they ridicule later change—then conceal its blessings.
translations.idiomatic: yet they smother every blessing visible after reforms.

sentences.zh: 漏見曲論，未可為是。

translations.literal: Leaked views and twisted doctrines—cannot be taken as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Such biased anecdotes cannot settle truth.

sentences.zh: 臣輒復重難衡、興，以為五紀論推步行度，當時比諸術為近，然猶未稽於古。

translations.literal: Your servant again repeatedly challenged Heng and Xing, considering that the Wuji lun’s extrapolated pacing degrees were closer than various techniques of the time—yet still not examined against antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I pressed Zhang Heng and Zhou Xing again: their Wuji lun solar theory beat rival schemes but still missed ancient benchmarks.

sentences.zh: 及向子歆欲以合春秋，橫斷年數，損夏益周，考之表紀，差謬數百。

translations.literal: When Xiang’s son Xin wished to match the Spring and Autumn Annals, he arbitrarily cut off year counts, diminishing Xia and augmenting Zhou—examining it against tables and records—errors numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin bent chronology to fit the Annals—trimming Xia and padding Zhou—and hundreds of years slip away.

sentences.zh: 兩歷相課，六千一百五十六歲，而太初多一日。

translations.literal: The two calendars mutually reckoned—six thousand one hundred fifty-six years—and Taichu had one extra day.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-comparing the systems over 6,156 years leaves Taichu one day long.

sentences.zh: 冬至日直鬥，而雲在牽牛。

translations.literal: On winter solstice day it is straight with the Dipper, yet they say it is in the Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Observation puts winter solstice in the Dipper while Taichu insists on the Ox.

sentences.zh: □闊不可復用，昭然如此。

translations.literal: [lacuna] vast—cannot again be used—thus brilliantly plain.
translations.idiomatic: The mismatch is gaping—Taichu cannot be revived—and plain as day.

sentences.zh: 史官所共見，非獨衡、興。

translations.literal: What the clerks together saw—not only Heng and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Every astrologer sees it—not only Zhang Heng and Zhou Xing.

sentences.zh: 前以為九道密近，今議者以為有闕，及甲寅元復多違失，皆未可取正。

translations.literal: Formerly one deemed the nine-path dense and close; now debaters deem it flawed; and the jiayin yuan again has many violations and misses—all are not yet able to take as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday’s nine-path consensus looks flawed today, and the jiayin epoch still disagrees with observation—none of these schemes earns final adoption.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼順假馬之名，以崇君之義。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhong Ni complied with the borrowed name ‘horse’ to exalt the lord’s righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius once accepted the courtiers’ euphemism ‘horse’ to uphold his ruler’s dignity.

sentences.zh: 況天之歷數，不可任疑從虛，以非易是。

translations.literal: How much more heaven’s calendar succession—one cannot indulge doubt and chase emptiness, using wrong to replace right.
translations.idiomatic: All the more must celestial reckoning reject groundless doubt—error cannot displace truth.

sentences.zh: 」上納其言，遂*[寢]*改歷事。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor accepted his words and then shelved the calendar reform.
translations.idiomatic: The throne adopted his advice and tabled further calendar change.

sentences.zh: 順帝漢安二年，尚書侍郎邊韶上言：「世微於數虧，道盛於得常。

translations.literal: In the second Han’an year of Emperor Shun, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Bian Shao submitted a memorial: ‘The age declines when reckoning loses ground; the Way thrives when constancy is grasped.’
translations.idiomatic: In Han’an 2, Attendant Clerk Bian Shao memorialized Emperor Shun that dynastic fortune weakens when calendrical constants drift but strengthens when they hold steady.

sentences.zh: 數虧則物衰，得常則國昌。

translations.literal: When reckoning fails, beings wither; when constancy is secured, the state flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Botched arithmetic breeds decay; faithful cycles sustain the realm.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝攄發聖思，因元封七年十一月甲子朔旦冬至，乃詔太史令司馬遷、治歷鄧平等更建太初，改元易朔，行夏之正，干鑿度八十*[一]*分之四十三為日法。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu unfolded sagely thought; because on the jiazi new moon at dawn of the winter solstice in the seventh year of Yuanfeng he ordered Grand Astrologer Sima Qian and calendar director Deng Ping and others to rebuild Taichu, change the era title and interchange new moons, practice Xia’s correct beginning, and take eighty-one forty-thirds from Ganzao du as the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, inspired by the Yuanfeng 7 winter-solstice new moon, commissioned Sima Qian and Deng Ping to forge the Taichu calendar—restoring the Xia calendar head, adopting Deng Ping’s 81-part day divisor from the apocryphal scale.

sentences.zh: 設清台之候，驗六異，課效觕密，太初為最。

translations.literal: He set up Qing Terrace observations, verified six anomalies, and reckoned efficacy coarse or fine—Taichu ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Observatory trials sorted rival schemes; Taichu proved tightest.

sentences.zh: 其後劉歆研機極深，驗之春秋，參以易道，以河圖帝覽嬉、雒書*

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Xin plumbed the mechanism deeply, verified it against the Spring and Autumn Annals, cross-referenced the Changes, and from the River Chart Di lan xi and the Luo document—
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin then harmonized the Annals and Changes with the Hetu Luoshu literature—

sentences.zh: 兩儀既定，日月始離。

sentences.zh: 初行生分，積分成度。

translations.idiomatic: Motion yields fractions; fractions stack into degrees.

translations.idiomatic: Solar motion is steady; tiny divisor errors explode across the sky.

sentences.zh: 自此言之，數無緣得有虧棄之意也。

translations.literal: From this speaking, numbers cannot have intent to abandon or waste.
translations.idiomatic: Arithmetic cannot sanction arbitrary discard.

sentences.zh: 今欲飾平之失，斷法垂分，恐傷大道。
