sentences.zh: **[午]*蔀之二十三歲，竟己酉、戊子及丁卯蔀六十九歲，合為二百七十五歲。

translations.literal: —‘wu’—bu’s twenty-third year—through jiyou and wuzi and ending at dingmao bu sixty-nine years—together two hundred seventy-five years.
translations.idiomatic: —linking sexagenary cycles to total 275 years down to Han’s foundation.

sentences.zh: 漢元年歲在乙未，上至獲麟則歲在庚申。

translations.literal: Han’s first year stands at yiwei; tracing upward to the unicorn year yields gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: Han began in yiwei; counting back lands on gengshen for the unicorn.

sentences.zh: 推此以上，上極開闢，則*

translations.literal: Extrapolate this upward to the limit of creation—then—
translations.idiomatic: Carry the sequence to cosmic genesis and—

translations.literal: The graph 不 is a miswriting for 元.
translations.idiomatic: Read 元 so the clause declares ‘the origin lies at gengshen.’

sentences.zh: **[元]*在庚申。

translations.literal: —‘origin’—lies at gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: —the universal epoch is gengshen.

sentences.zh: 讖雖無文，其數見存。

translations.literal: Although the prognostication lacks prose text, its numerology survives intact.
translations.idiomatic: Even without narrative glosses the arithmetic still checks out.

sentences.zh: 而光、晃以為開闢至獲麟二百七十五萬九千八百八十六歲，獲麟至漢百六十*

translations.literal: Yet Guang and Huang suppose from creation to unicorn two million seven hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred eighty-six years—from unicorn to Han one hundred sixty—
translations.idiomatic: Feng Guang and Chen Huang shorten creation-to-unicorn and unicorn-to-Han spans—

translations.literal: —two—
translations.idiomatic: —‘two’ completes ‘sixty-two’ incorrectly written—

sentences.zh: **[一]*歲，轉差少一百一十四歲。

translations.literal: —one years—turning the discrepancy short by one hundred fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: —yielding 161 years from unicorn to Han—114 years shy of canonical totals.

sentences.zh: 雲當滿足，則上違干鑿度、元命苞，中使獲麟不得在哀公十四年，下不及命歷序獲麟*[至]*漢相去四蔀年數，與奏記譜注不相應。

translations.literal: Claiming it balances would violate Ganzao du and Yuanming bao in the high reckonings, place the unicorn capture off Duke Ai’s fourteenth year mid-course, and fail below Mingli xu’s four-bu gap from unicorn to Han—matches neither memorial tables nor commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Their totals clash with every standard chronology.

sentences.zh: 當今歷正月癸亥朔，光、晃以為乙丑朔。

translations.literal: The present calendar’s first month begins on guihai new moon; Guang and Huang insist on yichou new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Official New Year opens guihai; they demand yichou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑之與癸亥，無題勒款識可與觿共別者，須以弦望晦朔光魄虧滿可得而見者，考其符驗。

translations.literal: Between yichou and guihai there is no inscribed tally by which to distinguish them with certainty—one must rely on phases whose waxing and waning can be seen to test correspondences.
translations.idiomatic: Only lunar phases can adjudicate guihai versus yichou.

sentences.zh: 而光、晃歷以考靈曜*[為本]*，二十八宿度數及冬至日所在，與今史官甘、石舊文錯異，不可考校；

translations.literal: Guang and Huang’s calendar takes Kaoling yao as its basis—the twenty-eight lodges’ degrees and winter solstice positions diverge from the Gan and Shi archives still kept—beyond reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: Their lodge spans and solstice clash with Gan De and Shi Shen.

sentences.zh: 以今渾天圖儀檢天文，亦不合於考靈曜。

translations.literal: Checking against the present spherical heaven instrument still disagrees with Kaoling yao.
translations.idiomatic: Modern armillary checks refute Kaoling yao too.

sentences.zh: 光、晃誠能自依其術，更造望儀，以追天度，遠有驗於圖書，近有效於三光，可以易奪甘、石，窮服諸術者，實宜用之。

translations.literal: If Guang and Huang could truly follow their own method, rebuild sighting instruments, pursue celestial degrees so that distant charts validate and the three luminaries match nearby—they could overturn Gan and Shi and silence every rival theory—in such a case they ought indeed to be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Let them build instruments that beat observation—then they may replace classical star tables.

sentences.zh: 難問光、晃，但言圖讖，所言不服。

translations.literal: When questioned, Guang and Huang cited only charts and prognostications—their answers did not convince.
translations.idiomatic: Under cross-examination they offered only apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 元和二年二月甲寅制書曰：『朕聞古先聖王，先天而天不違，後天而奉天時。

translations.literal: On jiayin in the second month of Yuanhe 2 an imperial rescript said: ‘I have heard that ancient sage kings anticipated heaven and heaven did not oppose them; they followed heaven and served its seasons.’
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang’s Yuanhe rescript repeats the sage-king formula before attacking Taichu.

sentences.zh: 史官用太初鄧平術，冬至之日，日在斗二十*

translations.literal: The clerks using Taichu Deng Ping’s method place the winter solstice sun at twenty—
translations.idiomatic: Taichu puts solstice at twenty—

translations.literal: —two—
translations.idiomatic: —‘two’ joins ‘twenty’ as twenty-one Dipper degrees—

sentences.zh: **[一]*度，而歷以為牽牛中星，先立春一日，則四分數之立春也，而以折獄斷大刑，於氣已迕，用望平和，蓋亦遠矣。

translations.literal: —one degrees in the Dipper, yet the calendar calls it mid-Ox; one day before Beginning of Spring is then the quarter-day Beginning of Spring—yet judging capital cases by it fights the qi; aiming at mild harmony is hopelessly remote.
translations.idiomatic: —restating Zhang’s indictment of Taichu misalignment.

sentences.zh: 今改行四分，以遵於堯，以順孔聖奉天之文。

translations.literal: Now we adopt the quarter-day system to follow Yao and Confucius’s model of serving heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth practice quarter-remainder reckoning as Yao and Confucius demand.

sentences.zh: 』是始用四分歷庚申元之詔也。

translations.literal: ’ This is the edict that first enacted quarter-remainder calendar with gengshen origin.
translations.idiomatic: That edict inaugurated gengshen quarter-remainder rule.

sentences.zh: 深引河雒圖讖以為符驗，非史官私意獨所興構。

translations.literal: It cited River and Luo apocrypha as verification—not a private whim of the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: It rested on canonical charts, not bureau caprice.

sentences.zh: 而光、晃以為*[香]*、固意造妄說，違反經文，謬之甚者。

translations.literal: Yet Guang and Huang think Guo Xiang and Liu Gu invented lies—utterly contradicting the texts.
translations.idiomatic: They accuse Guo Xiang and Liu Gu of forging doctrine against scripture.

sentences.zh: 昔堯命羲和歷象日月星辰，舜□時月正日，湯、武革命，治歷明時，可謂正矣，且猶遇水遭旱，戒以『蠻夷猾夏，寇賊奸宄』。

translations.literal: Ancient Yao charged Xi He to align sun, moon, and stars; Shun harmonized seasons and days; Tang and Wu changed dynasties while regulating calendars—all called correct—yet still faced flood, drought, and Hong fan warnings of barbarians and bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Even perfectly tuned calendars did not banish flood or rebellion.

sentences.zh: 而光、晃以為陰陽不和，奸臣盜賊，皆元之咎，誠非其理。

translations.literal: Yet Guang and Huang blame yin-yang discord and traitors on the calendar origin—that truly defies reason.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot blame banditry on the sexagenary epoch.

sentences.zh: 元和二年乃用庚申，至今九十二歲，而光、晃言秦所用代周之元，不知從秦來，漢三易元，不常庚申。

translations.literal: Yuanhe 2 adopted gengshen—ninety-two years on—and Guang and Huang call it Qin’s Zhou-replacement origin, unaware that since Qin Han has changed epoch thrice and never fixed on gengshen alone.
translations.idiomatic: Han has rotated epochs repeatedly since Qin; gengshen is not eternal.

sentences.zh: 光、晃區區信用所學，亦妄虛無造欺語之愆。

translations.literal: Guang and Huang cling credulously to their narrow learning—another species of empty fabrication.
translations.idiomatic: Their pedantry repeats the same fraud.

sentences.zh: 至於改朔易元，往者壽王之術已課不效，但誦之議不用，元和詔書文備義著，非腢臣議者所能變易。

translations.literal: As for changing the calendar head—Zhang Shouwang’s art already failed testing; Dan Song’s proposal was shelved; the Yuanhe edict is lucid and binding—not something court debaters may overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Prior failed reforms and the Yuanhe charter settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 太尉耽、司徒隗、司空訓以邕議劾光、晃不敬，正鬼薪法。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Dan, Minister of Education Kui, and Minister of Works Xun used Cai Yong’s memorial to impeach Guang and Huang for lese-majesty—punishable as convict labor.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes indicted Feng Guang and Chen Huang for disrespect.

sentences.zh: 詔書勿治罪[7]。

translations.literal: An edict declined to prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 太初歷推月食多失。

translations.literal: Taichu predictions of lunar eclipses mostly failed.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu eclipse math was loose.

sentences.zh: 四分因太初法，以河平癸巳為元，施行五年。

translations.literal: Quarter-remainder followed Taichu’s framework with heping guisi as origin and ran five years.
translations.idiomatic: The interim quarter scheme used a guisi epoch for five years.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，天以七月後閏食，術以八月。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan 1 heaven eclipsed the moon in the intercalary seventh month; the method placed it in the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Observation saw a seventh-month eclipse; tables said eighth.

sentences.zh: 其*

translations.literal: On—
translations.idiomatic: In—

translations.literal: —ten—
translations.idiomatic: —strike the erroneous 十 so ‘second year’ reads cleanly—

sentences.zh: *二年正月十二日，蒙公乘宗紺上書言：「今月十六日月當食，而歷以二月。

translations.literal: —second year first month twelfth day—the ranked commoner Zong Gan of Meng memorialized: ‘This month’s sixteenth day the moon ought to eclipse—but the calendar puts it in the second month.’
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth of month 1 in Yongyuan 2, Zong Gan predicted a month 1 eclipse while tables placed it in month 2.

sentences.zh: 」至期如紺言。

translations.literal: ’ At the appointed time it matched Gan’s words.
translations.idiomatic: The eclipse arrived as Gan predicted.

sentences.zh: 太史令巡上紺有益官用，除待詔。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Xun reported Gan useful to the office—removed expectancy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Xun recommended Gan and he became an expectancy-holder.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔書以紺法署。

translations.literal: On jiachen day an edict ordered Gan’s method applied.
translations.idiomatic: A jiachen edict adopted Gan’s tables.

sentences.zh: 施行五十六歲。

translations.literal: It was practiced fifty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: Gan’s scheme ran fifty-six years.

sentences.zh: 至本初元年，天以十二月食，歷以後年正月，於是始差。

translations.literal: By benchu first year heaven eclipsed in the twelfth month; the calendar placed it in the next year’s first month—then discrepancies began.
translations.idiomatic: Benchu 1 saw another mismatch between observation and calendar.

sentences.zh: 到熹平三年，二十九年之中，先歷食者十六事。

translations.literal: Down to Xiping 3, across twenty-nine years the calendar preceded eclipses sixteen times.
translations.idiomatic: Between those dates official predictions jumped ahead sixteen times.

sentences.zh: 常山長史劉洪上作七曜術。

translations.literal: Changshan Chief Clerk Liu Hong submitted his Seven Luminaries method.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong of Changshan offered his planetary theory.

sentences.zh: 甲辰詔屬太史部郎中劉固、舍人馮恂等課效，復作八元術，固等作月食術，並已相參。

translations.literal: On jiachen day an edict charged Masters of Writing Liu Gu, attendant Feng Xun, and others to test efficacy—again composing the Eight Origin method—Gu and colleagues composed lunar eclipse procedures—all mutually referenced.
translations.idiomatic: The court tasked Liu Gu and Feng Xun to cross-check Hong’s work with new eclipse algorithms.

sentences.zh: 固術與七曜術同。

translations.literal: Gu’s method matches Hong’s Seven Luminaries method.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gu’s math aligned with Hong’s.

sentences.zh: 月食所失，皆以歲在己未當食四月，恂術以三月，官歷以五月。

translations.literal: For eclipse misses—all agree year jiwei should eclipse in the fourth month—Xun’s method gives third month—official calendar fifth.
translations.idiomatic: For yiwei-year misses Feng Xun predicted month 3, the bureau month 5.

sentences.zh: 太史上課，到時施行中者。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer upward-tested—at arrival whichever matched observation prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau ran trials and favored whichever hit.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔書報可。

translations.literal: On dingsi day an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved on dingsi.

sentences.zh: 其四年，紺孫誠上書言：「受紺法術，當復改，今年十二月當食，而官歷以後年正月。

translations.literal: In that fourth year Gan’s grandson Cheng memorialized: ‘Having received Gan’s method—it ought change again—this year’s twelfth month ought eclipse—but official calendar places next year’s first month.’
translations.idiomatic: Zong Cheng refined his grandfather’s formula and challenged the next eclipse timing.

sentences.zh: 」到期如言，拜誠為舍人。

translations.literal: ’ At maturity it matched his words—Cheng was appointed supernumerary.
translations.idiomatic: The prediction succeeded and Cheng earned an appointment.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔書聽行誠法。

translations.literal: On bingshen day an edict authorized Cheng’s method.
translations.idiomatic: A bingshen edict adopted Cheng’s revision.

sentences.zh: 光和二年歲在己未，三月、五月皆陰，太史令修、部舍人張恂等推計行度，以為三月近，四月遠。

translations.literal: Guanghe 2, year jiwei—March and May were both cloudy—Grand Astrologer Xiu and section attendant Zhang Xun and others computed motions—judging March close, April remote.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds obscured two candidate nights in Guanghe 2.

sentences.zh: 誠以四月。

translations.literal: Cheng held April.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng favored April.

sentences.zh: 奏廢誠術，施用恂術。

translations.literal: They memorialized abolishing Cheng’s method—implementing Xun’s method.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau dropped Cheng for Xun.

sentences.zh: 其三年，誠兄整前後上書言：「去年三月不食，當以四月。

translations.literal: That third year Cheng’s elder Zheng repeatedly memorialized: ‘Last March saw no eclipse—it ought have been April.’
translations.idiomatic: Zong Zheng appealed that April was the true eclipse month.

sentences.zh: 史官廢誠正術，用恂不正術。

translations.literal: Astrological clerks discarded Cheng’s correct method—used Xun’s incorrect method.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau preferred Xun over Cheng.

sentences.zh: 」整所上*

translations.literal: ’ What Zheng submitted—
translations.idiomatic: Zheng argued—

translations.literal: —five—
translations.idiomatic: —correct the scribal 五 to 正 ‘proper.’

sentences.zh: **[正]*屬太史，太史主者終不自言三月近，四月遠。

translations.literal: —‘proper’—belongs to Grand Astrologer—the chief clerk never himself said March near and April remote.
translations.idiomatic: Proper protocol rested with the Grand Astrologer’s verdict.

sentences.zh: 食當以見為正，無遠近。

translations.literal: Eclipses ought take visibility as correct—there is no question of near or far.
translations.idiomatic: Observation—not arithmetic distance—settles eclipse timing.

sentences.zh: 詔書下太常：「其詳案注記，平議術之要，效驗虛實。

translations.literal: An edict went down to the Grand Master of Ceremonies: ‘Examine annotations closely—fairly debate each method’s essentials—verify truth or emptiness.’
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a neutral audit.

sentences.zh: 」太常就耽上選侍中韓說、博士蔡較、谷城門候劉洪、右郎中陳調於太常府，覆校注記，平議難問。

translations.literal: ’ Grand Master Jiu Dan forwarded Palace Attendant Han Shuo, Erudite Cai Jiao, Gucheng Gate Warden Liu Hong, and Right Gentleman Chen Diao to the ministry—to review annotations and debate.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers convened Han Shuo, Cai Jiao, Liu Hong, and Chen Diao.

sentences.zh: 恂、誠各對。

translations.literal: Xun and Cheng each replied.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xun and Zong Cheng presented defenses.

sentences.zh: 恂術以五千六百四十*

translations.literal: Xun’s method uses five thousand six hundred forty—
translations.idiomatic: Xun’s denominator counts five thousand six forty—

translations.literal: —days—
translations.idiomatic: —read 日月 ‘lunations’ instead of day alone—

sentences.zh: **[月]*有九百六十一食為法，而除成分，空加縣法，推建武以來，俱得三百二十七食，其十五食錯。

translations.literal: —‘months’—holding nine hundred sixty-one eclipses as divisor—yet removing fractional parts and vainly adding suspended methods—from Jianwu onward obtains three hundred twenty-seven eclipses—fifteen wrong.
translations.idiomatic: His eclipse canon miscounts fifteen of 327 eclipses since Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 案其官素注，天見食九十八，與兩術相應，其錯辟二千一百。

translations.literal: Examining the office’s standing annotations—heaven showed ninety-eight eclipses—matching both methods—the erroneous avoidance numbered two thousand one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Against ninety-eight observed eclipses his avoidance errors balloon.

sentences.zh: 誠術以百三十五月二十三食為法，乘除成月，從建康以上減四十一，建康以來減三十五，以其俱不食。

translations.literal: Cheng’s method takes every hundred thirty-five months twenty-three eclipses as rule—multiplying and dividing into months—from Jiankang upward subtract forty-one—since Jiankang subtract thirty-five—because both lack eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng’s interval arithmetic trims phantom eclipses before and after Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 恂術改易舊法，誠術中復減損，論其長短，無以相踰。

translations.literal: Xun’s method alters old rules—Cheng’s method trims further mid-course—judging their merits neither surpasses the other.
translations.idiomatic: Both schemes fiddle constants without decisive superiority.

sentences.zh: 各引書緯自證，文無義要，取追天而已。

translations.literal: Each cites charts and wefts to justify himself—the prose lacks essential meaning—only chasing heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They cite apocrypha yet aim only at fitting the sky.

sentences.zh: 夫日月之術，日循黃道，月從九道。

translations.literal: As for sun and moon arts—the sun follows the yellow path—the moon follows nine paths.
translations.idiomatic: Sun rides the ecliptic; moon follows lunar corridors.

sentences.zh: 以赤道儀，日冬至去極俱一百一十五度。

translations.literal: Using equatorial instruments—winter solstice distance from pole is uniformly one hundred fifteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Equatorial measures fix winter solstice polar distance at 115°.

sentences.zh: 其入宿也，赤道在斗中十一，而黃道在斗十九。

translations.literal: When entering lodges—the red path lies mid-Dipper eleven—the yellow path Dipper nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: Equator midpoints Dipper differently than the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 兩儀相參，日月之行，曲直有差，以生進退。

translations.literal: The two instruments cross-reference—sun and moon paths differ straight or curved—thereby producing advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Combining frames reveals why motions diverge.

sentences.zh: 故月行井、牛，十四度以上；

translations.literal: Therefore moon traveling Well and Ox exceeds fourteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Near Ox and Well the moon moves fastest.

sentences.zh: 其在角、婁，十二度以上。

translations.literal: When at Horn and Bond—twelve degrees or more.
translations.idiomatic: Near Horn and Bond it slows.

sentences.zh: 皆不應率不行。

translations.literal: Both fail uniform rates—cannot proceed solely by rule.
translations.idiomatic: Uniform rates fail along these arcs.

sentences.zh: 以是言之，則術不差不改，不驗不用。

translations.literal: From this speaking—unless techniques err they are not changed—unless unverified they are not discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Revise only after proved error.

sentences.zh: 天道精微，度數難定，術法多端，歷紀非一，未驗無以知其是，未差無以知其失。

translations.literal: Heaven’s Way is subtle—degrees hard to fix—methods multiply—calendar records vary—without verification one cannot know correctness—without discrepancy one cannot know fault.
translations.idiomatic: No criterion exists except empirical check.

sentences.zh: 失然後改之，是然後用之，此謂允執其中。

translations.literal: Once fault appears then change it—once correctness appears then use it—this is called faithfully holding the center.
translations.idiomatic: That is the doctrine of holding the mean.

sentences.zh: 今誠術未有差錯之謬，恂術未有獨中之異，以無驗改未失，是以檢將來為是者也。

translations.literal: Now Cheng’s method has no demonstrated fault—Xun’s method has no uniquely superior hit—using lack of verification to alter what has not failed means judging future guesses correct.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Cheng nor Xun yet proves decisive superiority.

sentences.zh: 誠術百三十五月月二十三食，其文在書籍，學者所修，施行日久，官守其業，經緯日月，厚而未愆，信於天文，述而不作。

translations.literal: Cheng’s method—every hundred thirty-five months twenty-three eclipses—the text lies in records—scholars cultivated it—practiced long—offices guard the craft—ordering sun and moon—thick yet not faulty—trusted in astronomy—transmitting without inventing.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng’s cycle is long-attested and conservative.

sentences.zh: 恂久在候部，詳心善意，能揆儀度，定立術數，推前校往，亦與見食相應。

translations.literal: Xun long served the observing department—detailed and well-intentioned—able to gauge instruments—establishing arithmetic—extrapolating forward and collating past—also matching observed eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xun’s observational skill matches eclipses too.

sentences.zh: 然協歷正紀，欽若昊天，宜率舊章，如甲辰、丙申詔書，以見食為比。

translations.literal: Yet harmonizing calendars and correcting eras—revering bright heaven—ought follow old statutes—like jiachen and bingshen edicts—taking observed eclipse as measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic precedent prefers eclipse testimony.

sentences.zh: 今宜施用誠術，棄放恂術，史官課之，後有效驗，乃行其法，以審術數，以順改易。

translations.literal: Now it is appropriate to implement Cheng’s method—discard Xun’s method—clerks shall test it—after later verification implement its law—to examine arithmetic—to comply with reform.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt Cheng until further tests dictate change.

sentences.zh: 耽以說等議奏聞，詔書可。

translations.literal: Dan reported Han Shuo’s consensus—the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Dan forwarded the verdict; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 恂、整、誠各復上書，恂言不當施誠術，整言不當復*

translations.literal: Xun, Zheng, and Cheng each memorialized again—Xun said Cheng must not be applied—Zheng said Xun must not again—
translations.idiomatic: The litigants appealed again—

sentences.zh: 三０二九頁七行出赤道北*[二十]*五度據集解引李光地說補。

translations.literal: Note: the figure should read “twenty-four degrees”; explanation follows.
translations.idiomatic: Editors settle on twenty-four degrees rather than twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 三０二九頁八行去極俱九十度當作「九十一度」，脫「一」字。

translations.literal: Page 3029, line 8: “distance from the pole in both cases ninety degrees” should read ninety-one; the graph “one” has dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: The lacuna fixes ninety versus ninety-one degrees from the celestial pole.

sentences.zh: 按：四分歷以周天為三百六十五度又四分一，赤道去極為其四分之一，約為九十一度。

translations.literal: Note: in the Quarter-Day Calendar the full circuit of heaven is taken as 365¼ degrees, and the equator’s angular distance from the pole is one quarter of that, roughly ninety-one degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Fractional Quarter reckoning implies about ninety-one degrees from pole to equator.

sentences.zh: 張衡渾儀謂「赤道橫帶渾天之腹，去極九十一度十六分之五，黃道斜帶其腹，出赤道表裡各二十四度，故夏至去極六十七度而強，冬至去極百一十五度亦強也」。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng’s armillary sphere states: “The equator girdles the belly of the armillary heaven at ninety-one and five-sixteenths degrees from the pole; the ecliptic crosses it obliquely and emerges twenty-four degrees inside and outside the equator on either side; hence at summer solstice the distance from the pole is a little over sixty-seven degrees, and at winter solstice a little over one hundred fifteen.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng gives pole-to-equator geometry and the twenty-four-degree ecliptic latitude.

sentences.zh: 上文亦言「冬至日去極一百十五度，夏至日去極六十七度，春秋分日去極九十一度」。

translations.literal: The passage above likewise says: “At winter solstice the sun is one hundred fifteen degrees from the pole; at summer solstice sixty-seven; at the spring and autumn equinoxes ninety-one.”
translations.idiomatic: Earlier lines already record the same solstice and equinox polar distances.

sentences.zh: 並足證當時以赤道去極為九十一度，黃道於牽牛及東井各距赤道南北二十四度也。

translations.literal: Together these fully confirm that the age took the equator’s distance from the pole as ninety-one degrees and the ecliptic’s separation from the equator at Ox and Well as twenty-four degrees north and south.
translations.idiomatic: The numbers align equatorial polar distance with ecliptic latitude at the relevant lodges.

translations.idiomatic: Editors add one particle while accepting synonymous variants.

sentences.zh: **[元]*在庚申集解引錢大昕說，謂自獲麟至開闢二百七十六萬歲，以六十除之，恰盡獲麟之歲，既是庚申，則開闢之始亦必庚申矣。

translations.literal: **[the origin]* lies in gengshen—the Jijie cites Qian Daxin, who says from unicorn capture to world opening is 2,760,000 years; dividing by sixty exhausts at the unicorn year gengshen, so world opening must also begin at gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin argues gengshen closure for the grand cycle.

sentences.zh: 當云「元在庚申」，「不」乃「元」字之鬥。

translations.literal: It should read “the origin lies in gengshen”; bu is a corruption of yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bu miswritten for yuan.

sentences.zh: 又引李銳說，謂上文雲二百七十六萬歲，尋之上行，復得庚申，「不」當作「復」。

translations.literal: It also cites Li Rui, who says the text above gives 2,760,000 years; tracing upward in the line again reaches gengshen—bu should read fu (“again”).
translations.idiomatic: Li Rui offers fu as another correction.

sentences.zh: 按：錢﹑李兩家之說並是，今從錢說改「不」字為「元」字。

translations.literal: Note: both Qian’s and Li’s views hold; now following Qian, bu is changed to yuan.

translations.literal: **[one]* year—the Jijie cites Li Rui, who says Cai Yong subtracted the years from jiayin opening to Han from the years from gengshen opening to unicorn capture, leaving 161 as unicorn-to-Han years, hence Guang and Huang fell short by 114 years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rui explains Yong’s subtraction and the 114-year gap.

sentences.zh: 今按：甲寅元開闢至獲麟積年二百七十五萬九千八百八十歲，獲麟至漢二百七十五歲，共二百七十六萬一百六十一歲，邕以庚申元開闢至獲麟積年二百七十六萬歲減之，則獲麟至漢為百六十一歲，明「百六十二歲」之「二」字當作「一」，今據改。

translations.literal: Note: jiayin opening to unicorn totals 2,759,880 years; unicorn to Han 275 years; together 2,760,161; Yong subtracted gengshen opening to unicorn (2,760,000), leaving unicorn-to-Han at 161—clearly “162” has two where it should be one; now emended.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong’s residual is 161 years from the unicorn omen to Han, not 162, so the second graph in the numeral is emended to the first, changing one hundred sixty-two to one hundred sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 三０三九頁一行下不及命歷序獲麟*[至]*漢相去四蔀年數據集解引盧文弨說補。

translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong questions ming lun.

sentences.zh: 三０三九頁一三行而光晃以為*[香]*固意造妄說據集解引盧文弨說補。

sentences.zh: 三０四０頁二行亦妄虛無造欺語之愆按：集解引盧文弨說，謂「亦」下文有鬥。

sentences.zh: 案下文云「以紺法署施行五十六歲」，自永元二年至本初元年，正得五十六年，故知「十」字衍也。

translations.literal: Case: below says “promulgated by the crimson method for fifty-six years”; counting from Yongyuan second year to Benchu first year yields exactly fifty-six years—hence the stray ten is redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative’s fifty-six-year interval confirms that the extra ten is a copying error.

sentences.zh: 今據刪。

sentences.zh: 三０四一頁二行部舍人張恂按：「張恂」疑當作「馮恂」。

sentences.zh: 上文言「熹平中，故治歷郎梁國宗整上九道術，詔書下太史，以參舊術，相應。

translations.literal: Above it says: “During Xiping, former calendar gentleman Zong Zheng of Liang submitted the nine-path method; an edict sent it to the Grand Clerk to compare with the old method—they agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Context from the preceding memorial.

sentences.zh: 部太子舍人馮恂課校，恂亦復作九道術，增損其分，與整術並校，差為近。

translations.literal: The department ordered heir-apparent attendant Feng Xun to examine it; Xun also reworked the nine-path method, adjusting its fractions; compared with Zheng’s method, the discrepancy was slight.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xun’s revision and comparison.

sentences.zh: 太史令揚上以恂術參朔望」。

translations.literal: Grand Clerk Yang Shang applied Xun’s method to conjunctions and full moons.”
translations.idiomatic: Closing the cited edict narrative.

sentences.zh: 此處雖言課校恂﹑誠二術，整為誠兄，且先後上書為誠術辨，則所謂整術﹑誠術實同為一事，而參與推計行度者為馮恂也。

translations.idiomatic: Cross-reference on sun omens.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕集載：「三月九日，百官會府公殿下，東面，校尉南面，侍中、郎將、大夫、千石、六百石重行北面，議郎、博士西面。

translations.literal: Cai Yong’s collected works record: “On the ninth day of the third month all officials assembled below the minister’s hall; the east faced the commandant of the guard, the south the attendant, general of the household, grandees, thousand- and six-hundred-bushel ranks in staggered rows to the north; deliberation gentlemen and erudites to the west.”
translations.idiomatic: Seating order at the calendar debate.

sentences.zh: 戶曹令史當坐中而讀詔書，公議。

translations.literal: The bureau clerk for households sat mid-hall and read the edict aloud for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure for reading the imperial charge.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕前坐侍中西北，近公卿，與光、晃相難問是非焉。」

translations.literal: Cai Yong sat forward northwest of the attendant, near the ministers, and argued back and forth with Guang and Huang over right and wrong.”
translations.idiomatic: Yong’s placement in the debate.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕命論曰：「顓頊歷術曰：『天元正月己巳朔旦立春，俱以日月起於天廟營室五度。

translations.literal: Cai Yong’s Treatise on the Mandate states: “The Zhuanxu calendar method says: ‘Heaven’s origin, first month, jisi new moon at dawn, Beginning of Spring—sun and moon alike rise from the Celestial Temple in Encampment at five degrees.’”
translations.idiomatic: Yong quotes Zhuanxu epoch placement.

sentences.zh: 』今月令孟春之月，日在營室。」

translations.literal: ’Now the Monthly Ordinance’s first month of spring places the sun in Encampment.”
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing Ordinance with Zhuanxu line.

sentences.zh: 臣昭曰：不有君子，其能國乎？

translations.literal: Your servant Zhao says: Without gentlemen, can there be a state?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhao’s editorial aside opens.

sentences.zh: 觀蔡邕之議，可以言天機矣。

translations.literal: Reading Cai Yong’s memorial, one may speak of Heaven’s hidden workings.
translations.idiomatic: Praise for Yong’s sophistication.

sentences.zh: 賢明在朝，弘益遠哉！

translations.literal: Worthy clarity at court extends benefit far!
translations.idiomatic: Commends the debate’s quality.

sentences.zh: 公卿結正，足懲淺妄之徒，詔書勿治，亦深「盍各」之致。

translations.literal: Ministers reached a just verdict—enough to chastise shallow bluster; the edict ordering no prosecution also honors the Analects’ “why not each follow his own course.”
translations.idiomatic: Outcome of the calendar controversy.

sentences.zh: 袁山松書曰：「劉洪字符卓，泰山蒙陰人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shansong’s Book states: “Liu Hong, courtesy name Zhuo, was a man of Mengyin in Taishan.”
translations.idiomatic: Biographical opening on Liu Hong.

sentences.zh: 魯王之宗室也。

translations.literal: He was of the cadet lineage of the kings of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong belonged to the Lu royal house.

sentences.zh: 延熹中，以校尉應太史征，拜郎中，遷常山長史，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: During the Yanxi era he answered the Grand Clerk’s summons as commandant of the guard, was appointed gentleman of the palace, promoted chief clerk of Changshan, then resigned on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi he entered imperial service through the astrological bureau, rose to Changshan chief clerk, and stepped down when his father died.

sentences.zh: 後為上計掾，拜郎中，檢東觀著作律歷記，遷謁者，谷城門候，會稽東部都尉。

translations.literal: Later he served as clerk for the commandery’s annual accounts reporting to the capital, was appointed gentleman of the palace, supervised editorial work on statutes and calendars at the Eastern Pavilion, advanced to herald, then ye gate watch officer and eastern-commandery commandant of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned via accounting clerk posts to history-office editorial duty on law and calendrics, then frontier and Kuaiji appointments.

sentences.zh: 征還，未至，領山陽太守，卒官。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he died en route before taking up concurrent stewardship as governor of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office before reaching his capital post as governor of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 洪善筭，當世無偶，作七曜術。

translations.literal: Hong excelled at reckoning, unrivaled in his age, and composed the Seven Luminaries treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong’s mathematics stood alone; he wrote on the seven celestial wanderers.

sentences.zh: 及在東觀，與蔡邕共述律歷記，考驗天官。

translations.literal: While at the Eastern Pavilion he collaborated with Cai Yong on the statutory calendar record and verified celestial offices.
translations.idiomatic: With Yong he compiled the calendar annals and tested officials’ sky lore.

sentences.zh: 及造干象術，十餘年，考驗日月，與象相應，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: When he devised the Qianxiang method, over ten years he tested sun and moon against the schema until observations matched theory—his work circulated thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: His decade-long Qianxiang revision aligned lunar and solar motion with observation.

sentences.zh: 」博物記曰：「洪篤信好學，觀乎六藝腢書意，以為天文數術，探賾索隱，鉤深致遠，遂專心銳思。

translations.literal: The Record of Wide Knowledge states: “Hong was devoted and fond of learning; surveying the meaning of the Six Classics and supplementary writings, he concluded astronomy and numerology plumb hidden depths and reach far horizons, so he bent his mind with keen concentration.
translations.idiomatic: Supplementary lore praises Hong’s classical breadth and dedication to calendrical inquiry.

sentences.zh: 為曲城侯相，政教清均，吏民畏而愛之，為州郡之所禮異。」

translations.literal: As minister of Qu prefecture his governance was fair and even; clerks and commoners feared yet loved him, and regional authorities singled him out for honor.”
translations.idiomatic: His tenure as Qu minister earned disciplined affection and official esteem.
